symptom: A pluggable widget .mpk copied into widgets/ after .mxcli/widgets had been populated passed check --references (packageInstalledFor finds the .mpk) while exec refused it: 'no definition for widget … its package is installed but not extracted yet (run mxcli widget init)'.
cause: RefreshStaleWidgetDefinitions, the auto-refresh both the page builder (initPluggableEngine) and check's registry (LoadProjectWidgetDefinitions) go through, extracted only when no .def.json existed or one had a generatorVersion behind the build; a new package beside current definitions matched neither case, so nothing was extracted and widget init was a hidden prerequisite.
fix: Third case: defs present and current -> non-forced RefreshWidgetDefinitions, which skips via refresh-state.json (a stat per mpk/def, no .mpk read) unless widgets/ or the defs changed, and then writes only new/changed definitions. Check already wrote this cache through the same function, so no new kind of write.
insight: Not a check/exec decision made twice: both shared the refresh, check just had a second, looser test (package installed) for the same widget. The fix belongs in the shared refresh, not in check's message. A refresh keyed on 'is anything stale' must also ask 'is anything new'; the state file #1848 added already answers that for the price of a stat. When verifying, rebuild-then-repro is not enough: a new binary changes the state fingerprint and forces a refresh by itself, so re-create the not-extracted state with the fixed binary.
test: mdl/executor/widget_defs_refresh_test.go TestRefreshStaleWidgetDefinitions_ExtractsPackageAddedLater (fails on origin/main with the new widget absent from the defs; control: the widget-init widget resolves and an unchanged widgets/ does no work)
